question: Which of the following alterations in amino acid metabolism is caused by a deficit of vitamin B12 ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "impaired conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA" -> "accumulation of methylmalonic acid" -> "methyl-malonic acidemia" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "impaired methionine synthesis" -> "possible homocysteine accumulation" -> "unclear link to phenylketonuric hyperphenylalaninemia" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "impaired methionine synthesis" -> "possible homocysteine accumulation" -> "unclear link to hypertirosinemia type I" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "impaired methionine synthesis" -> "possible homocysteine accumulation" -> "unclear link to alcaptonuria" -> 30%
analysis: Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to an accumulation of methylmalonic acid due to its role as a cofactor in the conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA. This results in methylmalonic acidemia. The other conditions listed are not directly related to vitamin B12 deficiency: phenylketonuric hyperphenylalaninemia is related to phenylalanine metabolism, hypertirosinemia type I is due to a deficiency in fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase, and alcaptonuria is caused by a deficiency in homogentisate oxidase.
